r1_cwd_p0_repaired.finding: The runner canonicalizes BASH_SOURCE[0] with readlink -f before changing cwd, validates the canonical location, and records the absolute self path in identity.sha256. Repository-root relative, hardware-root relative, and absolute invocations resolve to the same runner/root pair.

external_runner_trust_anchor.finding: Before any attempt is consumed, actual runner SHA must equal caller-supplied M510_EXPECTED_RUNNER_SHA256. The authorized caller value is the reviewed literal 0d05e6e668e6446575a6477ef7e151f9a6c459c275073ab0a789048915da8020; absent or mismatched values exit before attempt creation.

external_artifact_pinning.finding: Analyzer, contract-r2, docs510, docs359, r2 static-review SHA256SUMS and r2 review outer-seal file are hard-pinned. Review members and its nested seal are checked before attempt creation and again after audit.

identity_preflight.finding: All identity hashes are generated in a private mktemp file and immediately checked before atomic attempt mkdir. Failure or SIGTERM before mkdir leaves no consumed attempt; EXIT trap removes the temporary file.

single_owner_attempt.finding: mkdir of the fixed attempt directory is the atomic owner election. Only the winner moves the prevalidated identity file and proceeds; the durable attempt remains on every post-lock failure.

cwd_semantics.finding: identity.sha256 contains an absolute runner entry and hardware-root-relative artifact entries. Both the initial precheck and final sha256sum -c run with cwd fixed to the hardware root, so all entries resolve deterministically.

failure_cannot_be_pass.finding: set -euo pipefail prevents reaching POSTAUDIT_PASS after analyzer, output seal, input identity, or review seal failure. The PASS marker is written only after all those checks, then included in a final sealed attempt receipt.

final_output_and_input_recheck.finding: The analyzer output members and outer seal are checked; every pinned input and review member is checked again; identity.sha256 is revalidated; POSTAUDIT_PASS records the output outer-seal-file SHA.

p1_findings.finding: The final top-level receipt hashes SHA256SUMS.initial.seal.sha256 as a file, but the final block does not rerun sha256sum -c on that nested initial seal. The initial block did validate it, and the single-owner contract makes this non-blocking.
p1_findings.recommended_fix: Optionally recheck SHA256SUMS.initial and SHA256SUMS.initial.seal.sha256 immediately before emitting the final PASS receipt.

decision.condition: Caller must export the exact reviewed SHA literal above, observe attempt/output absent immediately before launch, and invoke this exact runner once.
